children: The US dollar index moderated as markets reduced expectations of a Fed rate hike later this month following a weaker-than-expected ADP report and dovish comments from Fed Governor Waller, HDFC Treasury Desk said.

The ADP report showed 38,000 job additions in August versus the market estimate of 47,000, while Waller said he supports holding the policy rate at the current level if inflation continues to progress towards the 2% target. The probability of a September rate hike has dropped to around 50% from around 70% last week.

The yen registered sharp gains against the US dollar, falling to the 155-156 range, "owing to intervention risk by Japanese authorities and amid rising bets for faster monetary policy normalization by the BoJ". Markets have also started pricing in rate hikes in September and October.

The focus now shifts to US NFP data. "While the market estimates 56K net job additions in August, up from -23K in July, any upside surprise could yet again increase the chances of a Fed rate hike, which could lead to some reversal in the US dollar index's recent losses," the report said.

On the domestic front, sentiment improved on strong dollar inflows under the RBI's special swap facility. "As of 31st August 2026, total dollar inflows under the special swap facility stood at $136 billion. This should provide the RBI adequate ammunition to limit extreme volatility in the pair."
"In the near term, we expect the pair to trade with an appreciation bias in the range of Rs 94.00-Rs 95.00," HDFC said. USD/INR appreciated 0.5% yesterday to close at Rs 94.4850.

Bond markets will watch for RBI liquidity absorption measures as banking system liquidity crosses Rs 9 lakh crore. The options being considered include "an FX sell/buy swap, a MSS facility, OMOs and an incremental CRR hike".
"We believe that the latter two could be less preferred at this stage and see a higher chance of a sell/buy swap apart from longer term VRRRs," the report said.

EUR/USD gained on broad US dollar weakness, while Eurozone PPI inflation rose to 5.8% in July versus the market expectation of 5.3%. HDFC expects the ECB to hike rates by 25 bps at its September 10 meeting and sees EUR/USD trading in the 1.1550-1.1650 range.

On USD/JPY, "the fundamental factors weighing on the pair remain in place, including elevated crude oil prices and a wide interest rate gap with the US". HDFC expects the pair to trade at 155-158, while "any upside surprise in today's US NFP data or further surge in oil prices could push the pair above the 158 level".
India's 10-year yield closed around 1 bp lower at 6.97%. The RBI did not accept any bids at the Rs 30,000 crore buyback auction. HDFC expects the yield to trade in the 6.90-7.05% range.

System liquidity surplus stood at Rs 9.70 lakh crore as of September 2. The RBI conducted two overnight VRRR auctions for a cumulative Rs 7.5 lakh crore, of which Rs 5.5 lakh crore was subscribed. "Given the surplus liquidity in the system, we expect the RBI to announce liquidity absorption measures over the coming days," the report said.

title: Dollar slips as Fed hike bets ease, HDFC sees USD/INR at Rs 94-95
